text: Then we turned and went up the road toward Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us with all his people to fight at Edrei.
But the LORD said to me, "Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
So the LORD our God also gave Og king of Bashan and all his people into our hand, and we struck them down until not a single survivor was left.
At that time we captured all his cities; there was not a town we did not take from them—sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All of these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides a great many unwalled villages.
We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, destroying every city—men, women, and children.
But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
So at that time we took the land from the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon—
the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, while the Amorites call it Senir—
all the cities of the plateau, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of Og's kingdom in Bashan.
For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was a bed of iron; it is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites, nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by the common cubit.

At that time we took possession of this land. I gave the Reubenites and the Gadites the territory from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, along with half the hill country of Gilead and its cities.

versions.text: At that time we took possession of this land. I gave the Reubenites and the Gadites the territory from Aroer on the Arnon Valley, along with half the hill country of Gilead and its cities.
versions.explanation: "Aroer on the Arnon Valley" is unclear when read aloud; the Hebrew אֲשֶׁר־עַל־נַחַל אַרְנֹן describes the town's position on the rim of the gorge. "On the edge of the Arnon Valley" is both more accurate and smoother.

text: The rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh—the whole region of Argob, all of Bashan. It used to be called the land of the Rephaim.

Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and he named that part of Bashan after himself, Havvoth Jair, which it is called to this day.

versions.text: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and he named it—that is, Bashan—after himself: Havvoth Jair, as it is called to this day.
versions.explanation: The double dashes and colon make this sentence hard to read aloud. The revised wording conveys the same sense (Jair named the Bashan settlements after himself) with a natural spoken rhythm.

text: And to Machir I gave Gilead.
To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the territory from Gilead down to the Arnon Valley, with the middle of the valley as the border, and up to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites,
along with the Arabah, bordered by the Jordan, from Kinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
At that time I commanded you: "The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your fighting men are to cross over armed ahead of your brothers, the Israelites.
Only your wives, your children, and your livestock—and I know you have much livestock—may remain in the cities I have given you,

until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as he has to you, and they too take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the property I have given you."
At that time I commanded Joshua: "Your own eyes have seen everything the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are about to enter.
Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God himself will fight for you."
At that time I pleaded with the LORD:
"Sovereign LORD, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your mighty hand. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do such deeds and mighty works as yours?
Let me cross over, I pray, and see the good land beyond the Jordan—that fine hill country and Lebanon."
But the LORD was angry with me because of you, and he would not listen to me. "Enough," the LORD said to me. "Do not speak to me about this matter again.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and look west and north and south and east. See it with your own eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.
But commission Joshua, and strengthen and encourage him, for he will cross over ahead of this people, and he will give them as their inheritance the land you will see.

versions.text: But commission Joshua, and encourage and strengthen him, for he will cross over ahead of this people, and he will give them as their inheritance the land you will see."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew pair is חַזְּקֵהוּ וְאַמְּצֵהוּ, "strengthen him and encourage him"; keeping the original order preserves the familiar word pair used elsewhere in the book.

text: So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth Peor.
